title: Keeping an LLM-voiced boss grounded during live combat: fighting or negotiating mid-fight in V.E.T.O.R — A Ruptura
author: Sufficient-Cause2216
selftext:
In our action-RPG project V.E.T.O.R — A Ruptura (currently in development for PC/Windows, no public demo yet), we wanted players and their onboard AI companion (V.E.T.O.R.) to be able to talk freely with an active boss mid-fight — without breaking combat rules or letting the LLM hallucinate quest state.

Here is an unscripted 4m44s run showing both combat and live negotiation against Voldrak the Troll: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HJMoPBQ2Wx4

How the AI pipeline stays locked to real game state:
- Live State Snapshot per Turn: Every utterance request sends Voldrak's current HP, active guard stance, stamina/temperament tier (Calm / Nervous / Fury), confirmed item inventory, and recent dialogue history so replies react to what is actually happening on frame.
- Hard Guardrails Against Fake Progression: Even if a player tries to trick the boss in free text, post-generation validation rejects outputs that claim an item was already handed over or that the trail is already open. Only an actual item transfer confirmed at the negotiation table unlocks passage.
- Anti-Repetition & Tone Filters: Replies that break third-person voice or echo earlier lines trigger a single regeneration pass (or stay silent rather than repeating canned lines).
- Voice-to-Combat Interrupt Sync: All PCM voice audio finishes buffering before Voldrak speaks so the silent MP4 talk clip aligns with output playback. Landing a strike mid-sentence suspends the Web Audio context and pauses the talk clip to play the damage reaction, then resumes both seamlessly once recovery clears.

Built on a custom HTML5 Canvas + synchronized video engine with real-time voice synthesis across 7 languages.

Project devlogs & updates: https://vetorlogico.com/#conheca-o-jogo

Happy to share implementation notes if anyone is working on LLM-to-gameplay state binding!
